translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets: “Look, I am sending my messenger before my face, who will prepare your way before you.”
“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole region of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, saying, “One stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
Immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens opening and the Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am well pleased with you.”
Immediately the Spirit led him out into the wilderness.
He was there in the wilderness for twenty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels served him.
After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of God,
saying, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the gospel of God.”
As he walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, that Simon’s brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
Going a little farther from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were also in a boat, mending their nets.
Immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and followed him.
They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he taught in the synagogue.
They were amazed at his teaching, for he taught as one who had authority, and not like their scribes.
In their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying, “Leave us alone! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are—the Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!”
And the unclean spirit shook him violently, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
And they were all amazed, so that they discussed it among themselves, saying, “What is this? What is this new teaching? For he commands even the unclean spirits with authority, and they obey him.”
And news of him immediately spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
And immediately, after leaving the synagogue, they came to the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon’s mother-in-law lay burning with a fever, and they immediately told him about her.
And he approached, took her by the hand, and raised her up. And the fever left her, and she served him.
When evening came, as the sun was setting, they brought all the sick to him.
And the whole town had gathered at the door.
And he healed many sick people who had various diseases, and drove out many demons. And he did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
And very early in the morning, at daybreak, he got up and went out. He went to a deserted place and prayed there.
And Simon and those who were with him went after him, and when they found him,
they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And he said to them, “Let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there too, for this is why I came out.”
And he preached in their synagogues throughout Galilee and drove out demons.
And a leper came to him, pleading with him and falling to his knees, and said to him, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
And Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be clean.”
And as soon as he had spoken, the leprosy left him, and he became clean.
And he sternly warned him and immediately sent him away.
And he said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. But go, show yourself to the high priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
But he went out and began to proclaim it widely and spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly, but stayed outside in deserted places. And people came to him from everywhere.
And after some days he went in again to him in Capernaum. And word spread that he was in the house.
And immediately many gathered, so that there was no longer room for them, not even in front of the door. And he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four people.
And because they could not get near him on account of the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. And after digging through it, they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak blasphemy like this? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were thinking this within themselves, said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—
“I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
He immediately got up, picked up his mat, and went out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
Jesus went out to the sea, and the whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As Jesus passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
While he was reclining at the table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many of them, and they followed him.
When the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Those who are healthy do not need doctors, but those who are sick do. For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in those days.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. Otherwise, the new patch pulls away from the old garment, and the tear becomes worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst them, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine must be poured into new wineskins.”
As he was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, his disciples began to make their way along, plucking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look, why are they doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?”
He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which only the priests were allowed to eat?”
Jesus said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
He entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They watched him closely to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
And he said to the man who had a withered hand, “Stand here in the middle.”
And he said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent.
Looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, whole like the other.
And immediately the Pharisees went out and plotted with the Herodians against him, discussing how they might destroy him.
But Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a large crowd from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,
and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan. A great multitude from the region of Tyre and Sidon, hearing about all that he was doing, came to him.
And he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing upon him, wanting to touch him.
And whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God.”
And he sternly warned them to make him known, for they knew that he was the Christ himself.
And he went up the mountain and called those whom he himself wanted, and they came to him.
And he appointed twelve to be with him and to send them out to preach, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray him.
And to have authority to heal diseases and to cast out demons.
And he gave Simon the name Peter.
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he gave them the name Boanerges, which means “Sons of Thunder.”
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew the tax collector, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean.
And they came into a house, and the crowds gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.
And when his own people heard about it, they went out to seize him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “He casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
No one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, all sins will be forgiven the children of men, and whatever blasphemies they may utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness; he is guilty
Everything happens.
So that, seeing, they may see and not perceive, and hearing, they may hear and not understand, when they turn back and their sins are forgiven.
And he said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How, then, will you understand all the parables?”
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word sown in their hearts.
Likewise, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy.
But they have no root in themselves and last only a short time. Then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
And these are the ones sown among thorns: those who hear the word.
But the worries of this age, the deceitfulness of wealth, and desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And these are the ones sown on good soil: those who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit, at [?]
And he said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?”
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor has anything been concealed except to be brought into the open.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.”
For whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
And he said, “The kingdom of God is like a man scattering seed on the ground.”
He sleeps and rises, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
For the earth produces fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the wheat in the ear.
But when the crop is ripe, he sends in the sickle, for the harvest has come.
And he said, “To what shall we liken the kingdom of God, or with what parable shall we describe it?”
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on earth.
And when it is sown, it grows and becomes larger than all the garden plants, and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his disciples.
And that day, when evening came, he said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side.”
After dismissing the crowd, they took him along, just as he was, in the boat. Other boats were also with them.
And a great windstorm arose, and the waves poured into the boat, so that it was already about to sink.
He himself was in the stern, asleep on a cushion. They woke him and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be silent! Be still!” And the wind died down, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, “Who, then, is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”
And they came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gadarenes.
And when he stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit immediately came from the tombs to meet him.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him, not even with an iron chain.
For he had often been bound with shackles and iron chains, but he tore the iron chains apart and broke the shackles, and no one could subdue him.
And continually, day and night, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and beating himself with stones.
But when he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
And he cried out in a loud voice and said, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me!”
For he had been saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
And he asked him, “What is your name?” And he said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
And he begged him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.
And all the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them.”

And Jesus immediately gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea. There were about two thousand of them, and they drowned in the sea.
And those tending the pigs fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside. And people came to see what had happened.
And they came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by demons, the one who had had the legion, sitting clothed and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them what had happened to the man possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to leave their territory.
And as he was getting into the small boat, the man who had been possessed by demons begged him to let him be with him.
But Jesus did not let him. Instead, he said to him, “Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.”
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
And when he had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him, and he was beside the sea.
And behold, one of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw him, he fell at his feet.
And he pleaded with him earnestly, saying, “My daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay your hands on her so that she may be healed and live.”
And he went with him. And a large crowd followed him and pressed against him.
And behold, there was a certain woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered much under many physicians and had spent everything she had, but had received no benefit at all and had instead grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.
For she was saying, “If I touch even his garment, I will be healed.”
And immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And immediately Jesus, sensing within himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
And his disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.
But the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And Jesus said to her, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace, and be free of your affliction.”
While he was still speaking, some people came from the synagogue leader, saying, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher?”
But Jesus, hearing what was said, said to the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only believe.”
And he allowed no one to follow him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
And he came to the synagogue leader’s house and saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
And he went inside and said to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The girl has not died but is sleeping.”
And they laughed at him. But he put them all outside and took the girl’s father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
And taking the girl by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Girl, I say to you, get up.”
And immediately the girl got up and walked, for she was twelve years old. And they were utterly astonished.
And he strictly ordered them that no one should know about this, and said, “Give her something to eat.”
He left that place and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were amazed at his teaching and said, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom given to him? And how are such mighty works done by his hands?”
“Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Are his sisters not here among us?” And they took offense at him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He could not do any mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He marveled at their unbelief. And he went around the small towns, teaching.
He called the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff—no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their belts.
They were to wear sandals but not put on two tunics.
He said to them, “Whenever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.”

“Whoever does not receive you or listen to you, when you leave that place, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them. Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom or Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They drove out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.
King Herod heard reports about Jesus, for his name had become well known. He said, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why mighty powers are at work in him.”
Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard this, he said, “It is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent men to seize John and had bound him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have the wife of your brother Philip.”
Herodias was angry with him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. After listening to him, he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.
An opportune day came when Herod held a birthday banquet for his officials, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
When the daughter of Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those dining with him. The king said to the girl, “Whatever you want, I will give you.”
He swore to her, “Whatever you ask, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She replied, “The head of John the Baptist.”
She immediately hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me the severed head of John the Baptist on a platter.”
And the king was deeply saddened, but because of his oaths and those dining with him, he did not want to refuse her.
And immediately the king sent a soldier and ordered him to bring his head.
He went and beheaded him in prison, brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl. And the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and everything they had taught.
And he said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a place alone, and rest a little.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
And many saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran there on foot from all the towns and arrived ahead of them.
And when Jesus came ashore, he saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
And when it had grown late, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and it is already late.
Send them away so that they may go into the surrounding settlements and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said to him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
And he said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and give.” And when they had found out, they said, “Five loaves and two fish.”
And he instructed them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
And they sat down in groups of a hundred and fifty.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people. And he divided the two fish among them all.
And they all ate and were satisfied.
And they gathered twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and some of the fish.
And those who had eaten the bread were five thousand men.
And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while he himself dismissed the crowds.
And after saying farewell to them, he went up the mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on land.
And he saw them struggling to row, for the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea, and intended to pass them by.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost and cried out.
For they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
And he got into the boat with them, and the wind died down. They were utterly amazed and terrified.
For they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened. And when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored there.
When they came out of the boat, the people immediately recognized him. They ran throughout that whole region and began bringing the sick on beds to wherever they heard he was.
And wherever he entered villages, towns, or fields, they laid the sick at the crossroads and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his garment. And all who touched him were healed.
The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
And when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with unclean hands—that is, unwashed hands—they found fault.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands, rubbing them, holding to the tradition of the elders.
And after the bath, they do not eat unless they wash themselves. There are also many other things they have received and hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, kettles, and beds.
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?”
He answered them, “Isaiah truly spoke well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments as doctrines.’
For you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition: washings of pitchers and cups. And you do many other things like these.”
And he said to them, “You are very good at rejecting the commandment of God so that you may keep your own tradition.
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might have received from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
violating the word of God through your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like these.”
And he called the whole crowd to him and said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
There is nothing outside a person that can defile him by entering him. Rather, the things that come out are what defile a person.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
And when Jesus had left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not understand that whatever enters a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and passes out through the latrine, expelling all the food?”
And he said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles him.
For from within, from the human heart, come evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual immorality, murders.
Thefts, acts of injustice, wickedness, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a person. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
And he rose and went from there into the regions of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know, but he could not remain hidden.
For a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, came, and fell at his feet.
The woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she answered him, “Yes, Lord, for even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
And he said to her, “Because of this answer, go. The demon has left your daughter.”
And she went home and found the girl lying on the bed, and the demon had gone out.
And Jesus again left the regions of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, through the region of the Decapolis.
And they brought him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking, and begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside, away from the crowd, put his fingers into his ears, and spat and touched his tongue.
And looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened.”
And immediately his ears were opened, the bond of his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
And he ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
And they were utterly astonished, saying, “He does everything well. He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples and said to them,
“I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them home without eating, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away.”
And his disciples answered him, “Where can anyone get enough bread to feed these people in this deserted place?”
And he asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
And he told the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve. And they set them before the crowd.
And they had a few small fish. He blessed these also and said, “Serve these too.”
And they ate and were satisfied, and they collected seven baskets of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand who had eaten. And he sent them away.
And immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, seeking a sign from heaven from him to test him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
And he left them, got into the boat again, and went to the other side.
And they forgot to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And he warned them, saying, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
And they discussed this with one another, saying, “We have no bread.”
“Why are you discussing the fact that you have no bread? Do you still not perceive or understand? Are your hearts hardened?
Though you have eyes, do you not see? And though you have ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of broken pieces did you take up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
“And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They said, “Seven.”
And he said to them, “Do you still not understand?”
And he came to Bethsaida. And they brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
And he took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. And he spat on his eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked him whether he could see anything.
And he looked up and said, “I see people; I see them walking like [?].”
Then he laid his hands on his eyes again and made him see. And he was restored and saw everything clearly.
And he sent him to his home, saying, “Do not go into the village or tell anyone in the village.”
And Jesus and his disciples went out to the village of Caesarea Philippi. And on the way he questioned his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say I am?”
And they answered, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others one of the prophets.”
And he said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered and said to him, “You are the Christ.”
And he strictly warned them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be put to the test by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and rise again on the third day.
And he spoke this openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying, “Get behind me, Satan! For you are not thinking about the things of God, but the things of human beings.”
And he called the crowds together with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.”
For whoever wants to save his soul will lose it, and whoever loses his soul for my sake and for the gospel will be saved.
For what does it profit a person to gain even the whole world and forfeit his soul?
For what can a person give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
And he said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come in power.”
And after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transfigured before them.
And his clothes became shining, exceedingly white like snow, whiter than any cloth cleaner on earth can make them.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking with Jesus.
And Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make two shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified.
And a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, he commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
And they kept this saying to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
And they asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered them, “Elijah does indeed come first and restore everything. And how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”
And when he came to the disciples, he saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
And immediately, when the whole crowd saw him, they were astonished and ran up to greet him.
And he asked the scribes, “What are you arguing about among yourselves?”
And someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a mute and deaf spirit.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. And I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
He answered, “O faithless generation, how long will I be among you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
And they brought him to Jesus. When the spirit saw him, it shook the boy violently, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
And Jesus asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” And he said to him, “Since childhood.”
And often it has thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us and have compassion on us.
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the child’s father cried out and said with tears, “I believe, Lord! Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus saw that a crowd was gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!”
And after crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. He became like a dead man, so that many said, “He is dead.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he stood up.
When he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
He said to them, “This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer and fasting.” They left there and traveled through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, and they will kill him. After he has been killed, he will rise on the third day.”
But they did not understand this saying and were afraid to ask him.
He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing among yourselves on the road?”
But they remained silent, for on the road they had been arguing with one another about who was the greatest.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”
He took a child and placed the child among them. Taking the child in his arms, he said to them,
“Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”
John answered him, saying, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name who does not follow us, and we stopped him because he was not following us.”
But Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him, for no one who performs a miracle in my name can soon afterward speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against you is for you.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you are Christians—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have both hands and go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have both eyes and go into fiery Gehenna.
Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not extinguished.
For everyone will be consumed by fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good. But if salt becomes saltless, with what will you salt it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves.
And from there [?] he came into the territory of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Crowds gathered around him again, and, as was his custom, he taught them again.
And the Pharisees approached and asked him whether it was lawful for a man to divorce his wife, testing him.
He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
Jesus answered them, “Because of your hardness of heart, he wrote this commandment for you.”
But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female. For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife.
And you two will become one flesh. So you are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has joined together, let no human being separate.
And in the house his disciples asked him about this again.
And he said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.”
And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.
And they were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked those bringing them.
When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.”
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.
And taking them in his arms [?], he blessed them, laying his hands on them.
As he was setting out on the road, a rich man ran up, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.”
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.
He answered him, “Teacher, I have kept all these things from my youth.”

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “If you want to be perfect, there is one thing you have not done. Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me; take up the cross.”
But he was dismayed at these words and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered them again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
They were even more astonished, saying to one another, “Who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “For human beings it is impossible, but not for God, for all things are possible for God.”
Peter began to say to him, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
Jesus answered, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who leaves a house, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or fields for my sake and for the gospel
who will not receive a hundredfold now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, and fields, with persecution—and in the age to come, eternal life.
Many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.”

They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them. They were amazed, and those following were afraid. Jesus took the twelve aside again and began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him, flog him, spit on him, and kill him, and on the third day he will rise again.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask.”
Jesus said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
They said to him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
It is not so among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you must be everyone's slave.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
They came to Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat blind beside the road, begging.
When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and said to them, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage. Get up; he is calling you.”
He threw off his clothes, got up, and came to Jesus.
Jesus said to him, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabbi, let me see again.”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he regained his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
When he approached Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it, and he will immediately send it back here.’”
The two went and found a colt tied outside by a door, at a crossroads, and they untied it.
Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
They answered them as Jesus had instructed, and the people let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus and laid their clothes on it, and he sat on it.
Many spread their clothes along the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them along the road.
Those going ahead and those following behind cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David, in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After looking around at everything, since it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next morning, when they had left Bethany, he became hungry.
Seeing a fig tree in leaf in the distance, he went to see whether he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing on it but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
Jesus said to it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” His disciples heard him.

They came again to Jerusalem. Jesus entered the temple and began driving out those selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
He would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
He taught them, saying, “Is it not written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
The scribes and chief priests heard this and looked for a way to kill him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, he went out of the city.
As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots. Peter remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered.”
Jesus answered him, “Have faith in God.”
Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Move and throw yourself into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, will have whatever he says.
Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you receive it, and it will be yours.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive anything you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your sins.
But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your sins.
And they came again to Jerusalem. While he was in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders came to him.
And they said to him, ‘By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?’
Jesus answered them, ‘I too will ask you one question. Answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Where did John’s baptism come from: from heaven or from men? Answer me.’
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, ‘If we say, “From heaven,” he will say, “Why then did you not believe him?”
But if we say, “From men”?’ For they feared the people, because everyone regarded John as a prophet.
And they answered Jesus, ‘We do not know.’ Jesus answered them, ‘Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.’
And he began to speak to them in parables: ‘A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, and built a tower. He leased it to tenant farmers and went away.
At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers to collect from them some of the vineyard’s fruit.
But they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent another servant to them. They struck him with stones, wounded him in the head, and sent him away in disgrace.
And again he sent another, and they killed him. He also sent many others; some they beat, and others they killed.
He still had one son, his beloved. He sent him to them last, saying, “They will respect my son.”
But when those tenant farmers saw him coming toward them, they said, “This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.”
And they seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this scripture: “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes”?’
And they sought to seize him, but they feared the crowd, for they understood that he had told the parable against them. So they left him and went away.
And they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to him to trap him in his words.

They came and said to him, ‘Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not defer to anyone, for you do not show favoritism, but teach the way of God in truth. Tell us, then, is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay or should we not pay?’
But he knew their hypocrisy and said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a coin so that I can look at it.”
They brought him one, and he said to them, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus answered them, “Give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.” And they were amazed at him.
Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying,
“Teacher, did not Moses write for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother?
There were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without leaving any offspring.
The second married her and died, and he too left no offspring. The third did likewise.
All seven married her and left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
At the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as their wife.”
Jesus answered them, “Is this not why you are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.

But concerning the dead, that they will rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. So you are greatly mistaken.”
One of the scribes came forward, having heard them debating and seen that he had answered them well, and asked him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus said to him, “The foremost commandment of all is: ‘Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the foremost of all the commandments.
And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher. You have spoken the truth: he is one, and there is no other besides him.

And to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is greater than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him any further.
While teaching in the temple, Jesus said in response, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David’s son?
For David himself said through the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”’
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?” And the large crowds listened to him gladly.

In his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes, receive greetings in the marketplaces, and have the foremost seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers for show. They will receive greater condemnation.”
And Jesus sat down opposite the treasury and watched how the crowd put money into the treasury. Many rich people put in large amounts.
And a poor widow came and put in two small coins, worth one quadrans.
And he called his disciples and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting money into the treasury.
For they all put in money out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had, her entire livelihood.”
And as he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look! What stones and what buildings!”
Jesus answered him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone here will be left upon another that will not be torn down.”
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew questioned him privately:
“Tell us, when will this happen, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus answered and began to say to them, “Be on your guard so that no one deceives you.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will deceive many.
When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and unrest.

These are the beginning of birth pains. But be on your guard. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues. You will stand before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them.
And the good news must first be proclaimed among all nations.

When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, nor rehearse it. Instead, say whatever is given to you at that hour, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
When you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Those on the roof must not come down into the house or enter to take anything from their house.
And anyone who is in the field must not turn back to get their clothes.
But woe to pregnant women and those nursing children in those days!
Pray that your flight will not take place in winter.
For those days will bring distress such as there has not been from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will be again.
And if the Lord had not shortened those days, no one would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he chose, he will shorten the days.
And if anyone then says to you, ‘Here is the Christ!’ or ‘Look, there he is!’ do not believe it.
For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders to lead astray, if they can, even the chosen.
But be on your guard. See, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that suffering, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
And the stars will begin to fall from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then you will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with great power and glory.
And then he will send his angels and gather his chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
Learn this lesson from the fig tree: when its branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know that the harvest is near.
So you too, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and hour, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but only the Father.
Be on your guard, stay awake, and pray, for you do not know when the time will come.
It is like a man going away: he left his house, gave his servants authority, assigned each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house will come—whether in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.
Otherwise, he may come suddenly and find you asleep.
And what I say to you, I say to everyone: stay awake.
Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. And the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, lest there be an uproar among the people.”

And while he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, reclining at the table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of costly perfume made from pure nard. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
But some were indignant among themselves and said, “Why was this perfume wasted?”
“For this perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good deed for me.”
“For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want, you can do good for them. But you do not always have me.”
“She has done what she could. She has anointed my body beforehand for burial.”
“Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray him to them.
When they heard this, they were glad and promised to give him silver coins. And he looked for a way to betray him at a suitable time.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying water in a pitcher will meet you. Follow him.
Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover meal with my disciples?’
He will show you a high upper room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”
The two disciples went out and came into the city. They found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he arrived with the twelve.
As they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with me will betray me.”
They began to grieve and to say to him one by one, “Is it I?” And another said, “Is it I?”
He answered them, “It is one of the twelve, the one dipping with me into the dish.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about him. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take it; this is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many.
Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink from the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.’
But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter said to him, “Even if everyone falls away, I will not.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today, this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But Peter spoke all the more insistently: “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And they all said the same.
They came to a village called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, “Sit here while I go and pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with him and began to be deeply distressed and troubled.
He said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
And he went a little farther, fell to the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass him by.
And he said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want.”
And he came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Could you not stay awake for one hour?”
“Stay awake and pray, so that you do not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
And he went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
And when he returned, he found them sleeping again, for their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he came a third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. The end has come. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.”
“Get up, let us go. Look, the one who betrays me is near.”
And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and lead him away securely.”
And when he arrived, he immediately approached him and said, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” And he kissed him.
And they laid hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing nearby drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
And Jesus said to them in response, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber?”
“Every day I was among you, teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me. But let the Scriptures be fulfilled.”
And they abandoned him and fled.
And a certain young man followed him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seized the young man.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
And they led Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes gathered around him.
And Peter followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the servants and warmed himself by the firelight.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they could find none.
For many gave false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree.
And some stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying,
“We heard him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made by human hands, and in three days I will build another, not made by human hands.’”
Yet even so, their testimony did not agree.
The high priest stood up in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Do you make no answer? What is this testimony they are giving against you?”
But Jesus remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest questioned him, saying to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
The high priest tore his robes and said, “What further testimony do we need?”
“You have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?” And they all condemned him as deserving death.
Some began to spit on him, cover his face, torment him, and say to him, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who struck you?” And the servants took him and struck him on the cheek.
While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls came.
Seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
But he denied it, saying, “I neither understand nor know what you are saying.” He went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
Another servant girl saw him again and began saying to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “You really are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech matches.”
But he began to invoke curses and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
The rooster repeated its call and crowed a second time. Peter remembered the words Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he began to weep.
Immediately in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council. They bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate questioned him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”
The chief priests made many accusations against him, but he gave no answer.
Pilate questioned him again, saying, “Do you make no answer? Look how much testimony they are giving against you.”
But Jesus gave him no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
At every festival he would release for them one prisoner whom they requested.
There was a man called Barabbas, imprisoned with his fellow conspirators, who had committed murder on the mountain.
The crowd cried out and began asking him to do as he usually did for them.
Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests urged the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
Pilate answered again, “What, then, do you want me to do with the one you call the King of the Jews?”
But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they shouted even more, “Crucify him!”
Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas to them. After having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers led him inside the courtyard, that is, the praetorium, and called together the whole cohort.
They clothed him in purple, wove a crown of thorns, and put it on him.
And they began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck him on the head with a reed and spat on him, and they bent their knees and bowed before him.
When they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple robe, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him out to crucify him.
They compelled a passerby, a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which means “Place of the Skull.”
They offered him sour wine to drink, but he did not accept it.
After crucifying him, they divided his clothes, casting lots for them to decide who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
The inscription stating the charge against him read, “The King of the Jews.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, “He was counted among the lawless.”
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
save yourself and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests, together with the scribes, mocked him, saying to one another, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down from the cross now, so that we may see and believe.” Those crucified with him also taunted him.
When the sixth hour came, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lima zavachthani,” which means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some of those standing nearby heard this and said, “Look, he is calling Elijah.”
One man ran, filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink, saying, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
Jesus gave a loud cry and breathed his last.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing opposite him saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God.”
There were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
When he was in Galilee, these women followed him and served him. There were also many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And evening had already come, since it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath.
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected member of the council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised that he had already died. He summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had died.
And after learning this from the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
And Joseph bought a linen cloth, took him down, and wrapped him in the linen cloth. He laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock and rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses watched where he was being laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could go and anoint him.
And very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
And they were saying to one another, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”
And when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
And when they entered the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, here is the place where he was laid.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee. And there you will see him, just as he told you.”
And they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and amazement had seized them. And they said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
After rising early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him, who were mourning and weeping.
But when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe it.
After this, he appeared in a different form to two of them as they were going into the countryside, walking into the countryside.
And those two went and told the others. Nor did they believe those two [?].
